1178394775617249285.a:
The hardest part of running a datacenter for many years was perimeter security. Distrust of hardware/software, isolation, and prestidigitation proved the best strategies. e.g. "Czech Republic" attackers would waste weeks of effort if you gave them a weak SSH port into a honeypot. Tweet by @DebugPrivilege

https://x.com/DebugPrivilege/status/1178386703897239552

1178395420449558530.a: Honeypots were very useful. They cost very little on a VM-based system. Dedicate some junk hardware to their cause. Give them a super slow link to the Internet. Fake ICMP. Snapshot often. Put them on their own VLAN that looks real. They will show you their techniques unwittingly.

1178396405444075523.a: A roach motel for infiltrators. They tend to be so arrogant they have no idea they are in a cage...in the wrong datacenter. Let them do their thing, limit damage to inside the cage, and later analyze the snapshots they unwittingly left behind to harden your real infrastructure.

1178397340937445378.a: IPv4 was all about the perimeter. In a world of IPv6 everything is on the Internet. Everything must be assumed compromised. @QubesOS is an excellent example of an operating system that gets this. Using it can at least teach you how to live under such threat.
